title: Derived common-quotient reduction as a normalized strict tower
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:R\to B$ a flat morphism of commutative ring sheaves, and $J_1\supseteq J_2\supseteq\cdots$ ideal sheaves of $R$. Assume the maps induced by $\varphi$ identify $S_n=R/J_n$ with $B/J_nB$, compatibly with quotient transitions. Use the module categories, restriction, derived categories and K-flat derived scalar extension of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every $M\in D(B)$ there are canonical $S_n$-linear isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Res}M\otimes_R^L S_n\cong M\otimes_B^L S_n.$$
Choose a single K-flat $B$-representative $P$ with flat terms. These isomorphisms are induced by the ordinary comparisons $\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_R S_n\cong P\otimes_B S_n$, both identified with $P/J_nP$, and are natural in $M$. After restriction of all levels to $R$, the comparisons form an isomorphism of strict tower complexes, commute with all quotient transitions, and carry the strict quotient cone $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ to the corresponding cone. Here tensor products and their pure sections are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], and K-flatness and flat terms are [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. A strict tower here means an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] in the category of cochain complexes of sheaves of $R$-modules; its cone is a morphism from the constant tower on $\operatorname{Res}P$.

proof.text: Obtain the ordinary normalized scalar comparison, transitions and quotient units from [lem-weil-pbc-ordinary-common-quotient-tower]. Lift the ordinary natural isomorphisms termwise with Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso.

Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits by the existing exact restriction lemma in [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings-independent]. Tensor comparison identifies the underlying scalar extension with tensoring by Res B. Flatness therefore makes extension exact. For a K-flat B-complex P and an acyclic R-complex F, extension of F is acyclic. Apply braiding to the ordinary tensor cancellation on both sides, obtaining Res(extension(F) tensor_B P)≅F tensor_R Res(P) in each bidegree. Naturality in the two variables identifies both bicomplex differentials. Exact restriction commutes with the total complex, so the total comparison gives the acyclicity required for K-flatness of Res(P), without constructing a signed total-complex symmetry. This K-flat claim is proved privately in Lean rather than imported from the absent flat-restriction module.

Choose a representative G of M in D(B) and a flat-term K-flat resolution P→G. Its localization gives Q(P)≅M. Transport monoidal flatness through the site tensor comparison to obtain exactly IsFlatOnSite of each term.

Compose the exact-restriction localization comparison, the R-side derived counit and the ordinary cochain comparison to a natural transformation β from Q followed by Res-derived followed by a.T to b.EComplex followed by Q. The universal left-derived property of b.T gives δ with δ(QP) followed by b.ε(P)=β(P). On K-flat P both counits and the ordinary comparison are isomorphisms, so δ(QP) is iso. Every derived object has a K-flat representative, hence all components of δ are iso. This yields the desired derived comparison and the exact counit normalization, in fact at all complexes.

Restrict the ordinary cochain comparisons to R and call them e_n. Lift the ordinary transitions degreewise to tL_n, and define tR_n=e_(n+1)^(-1) tL_n e_n. Functor.ofOpSequence and NatTrans.ofOpSequence give a strict tower isomorphism. The inverse pure-section formula follows from e_n e_n^(-1)=1, proving the required formula for tR. Lift the ordinary units degreewise and use their transition equation to construct ηL; put ηR=ηL e. The ordinary formulas prove both unit formulas, epi and the exact local ideal-product kernel. Thus every field of Comparison is filled.

proof_origin.place: T5 Lean reduction: separate ordinary quotient calculation, prove flat restriction by tensor cancellation, descend via the existing cochain model universal property, and explicitly assemble normalized strict towers. Exact restriction reuses the existing coefficient-change API; ordinary braiding orders cancellation before totalization.
